trick-or-think.title: Trick or Think?
trick-or-think.description: Ten Halloween questions. A few familiar things might surprise you.

questions.prompt: Before pumpkins, what did people in Ireland carve into Halloween lanterns?
questions.explanation: Turnips made the spooky faces. The National Museum of Ireland keeps a model of a traditional turnip lantern.

source.title: National Museum of Ireland: Ghost turnip

questions.prompt: The name Halloween is linked to which older name?
questions.explanation: All Hallows' Eve is the evening before All Saints' Day, also called All Hallows, on 1 November.

questions.prompt: A bat flaps past the window. What kind of animal is it?
questions.explanation: Bats are mammals. They are the only mammals capable of sustained flight, rather than gliding.

questions.prompt: 'Blind as a bat' sounds convincing. Is it true?
questions.explanation: Bats can see. Their vision varies, and many species also use echoes to find their way.

questions.prompt: When a bat uses echolocation, what bounces back to its ears?
questions.explanation: The bat makes calls and listens for returning sound. Those echoes help it locate objects and prey.

questions.prompt: Check that Halloween spider decoration. How many legs should an adult spider have?
questions.explanation: Eight legs. Insects have six, so a spider is not an insect.

questions.prompt: Your pumpkin has a less spooky family connection. It belongs with which plants?
questions.explanation: Pumpkins, squashes and gourds are cucurbits. Some varieties even belong to the same species.

questions.prompt: A pumpkin plant's first flowers often make no pumpkins. What is a common reason?
questions.explanation: The first flowers are usually male. The small developing fruit sits at the base of a female flower.

questions.prompt: A calendar calls a full Moon a 'Blue Moon'. Must it look blue?
questions.explanation: No blue paint needed. In its common modern use, the name means the second full Moon in a calendar month.

questions.prompt: An owl turns its head to look around. Why does that help?

options.label: Its eyes are on its wings
Its ears cannot hear behind it
Its eyes cannot move in their sockets
It is changing the colour of its eyes

questions.explanation: Owl eyes stay fixed in their sockets. A flexible neck helps the bird look in different directions.

spooky-connections.title: Spooky Connections
spooky-connections.description: Sixteen words. Four hidden groups. Can you untangle them?

groups.label: Parts of a skeleton
groups.explanation: A skull, rib, femur and pelvis are all parts of a skeleton.

groups.label: Words after 'ghost'
groups.explanation: Ghost town, ghostwriter, ghost story and ghost ship.

groups.label: Sounds in a spooky night
groups.explanation: A hoot, a howl, a rustle and a creak: four sounds that can make a quiet night feel spooky.

groups.label: Something sweet
groups.explanation: Fudge, toffee, liquorice and chocolate are sweets. Treat yourself to that connection.
